PAYO.gist: A stock in an uptrend below resistance (the top of its 10-week base); a daily close above it starts the move.

standouts.head: An ascending triangle
standouts.text: Sellers have capped it at the same level twice while each dip stops higher: pressure building under the ceiling.
standouts.learn: A flat ceiling with rising lows: buyers keep paying more.

standouts.head: Holding its rising 50-day
standouts.text: It dipped to its rising 50-day average in the last three sessions and held above it.
standouts.learn: The average close of the last 20, 50 or 200 sessions; rising averages mark uptrends and often act as support.

standouts.head: A higher high and a higher low
standouts.text: Its last swing high and swing low each topped the one before.
standouts.learn: A swing high above the one before and a swing low above the one before: the steps of an uptrend.

standouts.head: Momentum holding a bull range
standouts.text: RSI has stayed above 46 on every dip for three months and reached 75: the range momentum holds in an uptrend.
standouts.learn: In uptrends RSI tends to hold 40 on dips and reach 70; in downtrends it fails near 60 and reaches 30.

against.head: Buying is losing force (weekly)
against.text: On the weekly chart, price made a higher high the week of Sep 21 while 6 of 7 momentum gauges made a lower high (regular bearish divergence).
against.learn: Price makes a higher high but momentum makes a lower high: buyers are tiring.

against.head: A thin rise
against.text: Volume on the current rise runs 59% below its 50-day average: few buyers behind it.
against.learn: A rise on heavy volume has buyers behind it; a thin rise often fades.

against.head: A pullback that is not done
against.text: The pullback from the Sep 25 high is not done: it has not reached the 0.5 retracement and it is too quick for the advance before it. A wave 2 usually takes three waves and reaches the 0.618–0.786 of the Mar 2–Sep 25 advance (−26% to −34%).
against.learn: A real wave 2 takes three waves and time, on lighter volume. Too shallow, too quick, one straight leg or rising selling says it has further to go.

PAYO.take: PAYO: it is in an uptrend on every average, below resistance at the top of its 10-week base; the buy waits for a daily close above it. There is an ascending triangle, and it is holding its rising 50-day. Against it, buying is losing force (weekly). The desk is for it.
PAYO.change: No trade until a daily close above +0.6%; once in, a daily close below +0.3%, under the top of its 10-week base, proves it wrong.

standouts.head: Confirmed double bottom

standouts.head: Downtrend broken: over its last swing high
standouts.text: The swings had been falling, but price has closed over the last swing high (Sep 21): the run of lower highs is broken.

standouts.head: MACD positive

against.head: A descending triangle

against.head: Uptrend structure broken, then reclaimed
against.text: On Aug 28 it closed under the Jul 31 higher low, ending the run of higher lows, and it has closed back over that low since; the larger swings (4 ATR) are intact.

standouts.head: A deep wave 2
standouts.text: Five clean waves up from Apr 7 to Jul 16 (+75%, wave 1). The pullback is under the 0.618–0.786 zone of that advance (+16% to +4.5%), in three waves, with the 50-day average and the 50-week average in the same place. standouts.head: Momentum holding a bull range
standouts.text: RSI has stayed above 51 on every dip for three months and reached 81: the range momentum holds in an uptrend.
standouts.learn: In uptrends RSI tends to hold 40 on dips and reach 70; in downtrends it fails near 60 and reaches 30.

standouts.head: Quiet selling on the dip
standouts.text: Volume on the current pullback runs 22% below its 50-day average: profit-taking, not an exit.
standouts.learn: A dip on light volume is profit-taking; a dip on heavy volume is selling.

against.head: Weekly: five waves up look complete
against.text: On the weekly chart: five clean waves up from Dec 20, 2021 to Oct 19 (+337%), and the fifth wave's high came on weaker momentum than the third's (RSI 78 against 82 on Sep 14). A finished five is usually followed by a pullback, often to the 0.382–0.618 of the advance (−25% to −45%): the buy is the next wave 2, not this high.
against.learn: A fifth wave that makes a new high on weaker momentum than the third often ends the advance; the next buy is the pullback after it, not the high.

against.head: Buying is losing force

material.head: Weekly: wave 4 turning up from its zone
material.text: On the weekly chart: waves 1 to 3 up from Feb 9 to Aug 17 (+63%; wave 3 is 1.6 times wave 1). The pullback turned up from the 0.382–0.5 zone of wave 3 (−5.1% to −9.7%), in three waves, on lighter volume, with the 50-week average and the Apr 20 high in the same place. The count is wrong on a daily close under the wave-1 high (−8.3%): wave 4 never overlaps wave 1.

against.head: Weekly chart: declining
against.text: On the weekly chart price is below a falling 30-week average: the declining stage.
against.learn: Stocks cycle through basing, advancing, topping and declining; the advancing stage (above a rising 30-week average) is where longs pay.

against.head: The trigger failed before
against.text: It closed above this line 3 times since Sep 28 and gave it back each time.
against.learn: A line price closed above and then gave back has failed once already; the next break has to hold to count.

PZZA.take: PZZA: it is in a downtrend on every average; the buy waits for a daily close above the 20-day average, the first sign the decline is over. The stochastic is leaving oversold. Against it, it is in a downtrend on every average. The desk stays out until the trigger's close says otherwise.
PZZA.change: Until a daily close above +7.2%, the decline is intact and there is no trade; once in, a daily close below +2.9%, under the 20-day average, proves it wrong. The case against, that it is in a downtrend on every average, fails on a daily close above +16%, the 50-day average.
